While the benchmark runs: ready your real summary
Phase 5: Run it on something real

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 1 line 19 "Then join the team lead's screen when the scoreboard lands in phase 3." (scoreboard first named here, but the lede line 7 names the scorer that measures and it is a session artifact of the exercise per the carve-out); chunk 7 line 106 "It found something" resolves to "a file you can run" in the same sentence. Harm (unresolvable referent on a projected slide) absent.
No pointer to another file by position. Closest: chunk 1 line 11-15 "your curator's synthesis note" names a document by title, not position. Harm (callback aimed at whichever opener precedes) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Backward refs: line 64 "the four methods aloud from the phase 2 files" -> chunk 3 writes four files (lines 41-52); line 68 "Turn the post-its over" -> line 64; line 102 "the claim you bet on" -> line 15. All resolve in-file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 3 "Phase 2: Run four checks": line 41 "Four checks, four methods, the same claim pool, each in its own subagent, each writing to its own file." and line 43 "Four of them fanning out at once over the evidence." carry no finite verb: a muted read gets a set list and a scene for the live fan-out, not a sentence. Harm (§28(a) cue fragment: the room hears a scene, the deck reader a list) is present; no maintainer accept-note covers them and neither follows a verbed sentence naming the set.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Give line 41 a verb and subject ("Four checks run on the same claim pool, each as its own subagent writing to its own file.") and line 43 likewise ("The four fan out at once over the evidence.")

rules_evaluated.evidence: Every chunk carries a claim. Closest: chunk 1 line 19 "Then join the team lead's screen when the scoreboard lands in phase 3." is a one-line handoff but sits under a full chunk of instruction (lines 11-17).
Closest: chunk 1 header "While the benchmark runs: ready your real summary" (line 11); body is exactly that task, so the header is literally true.

chunk 2 "Phase 1: Plant the claims" line 29: "Aim for roughly one claim in ten made up or stretched. Claude cannot hit that number exactly." is the number + own retraction sub-item; the maintainer block carries no attest. Other sub-items clean: no Not X/Not Y, no anaphora triple (line 96 "The briefing was built to be caught. Your real summary was not." is a pair), no self-grading superlative, no verb triplet.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Pick the claim: label the number as a direction in one sentence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep dialect (surface|firing|compendium|forcing|beat|mood) in body lines 1-107 -> 0 hits (only maintainer lines 110-127 hit). Closest: line 41 "detector"/"scorer" are exercise vocabulary the prompts define, what the room calls them.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Bold in body: line 5 "**What you do:**" (chunk 0) and line 31 "**Don't open the briefing.**" (chunk 2, 5 words, one per slide). Closest: line 31 is a whole sentence but within the 5-word handle cap and a single element.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All body content sits under `##` headings of an exercise file (chunks 1-7, lines 11-106) with no phase-less prose section; lede lines 1-9 are chunk 0 title slide.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise headings are phase labels or imperatives: line 11 "While the benchmark runs: ready your real summary", lines 21-92 "Phase 1: Plant the claims" ... "Phase 5: Run it on something real", line 104 "Take stock". Closest: "Take stock" is imperative, not a declarative claim, correct for an exercise close.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 7 line 106 recap "Four checks ran, a scorer measured them, ..." could read as doctrine restatement, but it names the artifact kept and its Known limit line, a close the exercise owes; line 102 '"The agent got this wrong" is the sentence.' is a move, not a koan.
